notes: Worktree check: HEAD is refs/heads/sprint/r-3-shared-http, which resolves to 8f969ff85e09091da65dc5153425e36cef3e9de8. This matches the assigned commit. I only had read tools (no shell), so no tests were run. The ureq redirect behaviour below was checked against the vendored ureq 3.5.1 source.

RSH-005 stays CLOSED. crates/sc-agent-http/src/retry.rs now has the 90 s budget (BUDGET), jitter up to 250 ms on every wait, and cancellation checked before every send and between wait slices of at most 100 ms (WAIT_SLICE). Evidence: retry.rs:62, 59, 65, 259, 201.

RSH-006 stays CLOSED. UreqTransport::new builds one ureq Agent via AgentConfig::build, and clones share it (ureq_transport.rs:47-57, 105-110). The agent sets connect timeout 10 s, global timeout 120 s, max_redirects 0, https_only and a versioned User-Agent. The unit test test_ureq_agent_config_values and the loopback test test_agent_is_reused_across_sends (one keep-alive connection for three sends, including a clone) cover it.
Owner decisions encoded exactly, from the code:
- Busy statuses are exactly 429, 502 and 529 (BUSY_STATUSES, unit test busy_set_is_exactly_three_statuses). The default is 4 sends, and the same Arc<[u8]> body is resent.

- Retry-After uses a strict grammar. It must be 1-32 bytes matching ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$. The integer part is parsed with saturating arithmetic, so no float, sign, exponent, inf or NaN is possible. A 32-digit value saturates to the 30 s clamp and a 33-digit value is malformed. Tests cover both cases. A valid value is clamped to 0-30 s.
- An absent or malformed header backs off 1, 2, 4 s (cap 30 s). The wait is min(base + jitter, budget remaining). When no budget remains no further attempt starts.

- The two exhaustion errors are distinguishable. Both are NETWORK_ERROR kind Busy and retryable, but the details read "N sends exhausted" and "retry budget exhausted" (tests/retry.rs test_exhaustion_reason_distinguishable).

- A transport error is returned immediately with no retry. That covers connect, DNS, timeout, a failure after the body was sent, and an oversize body. There is no connectivity probing and no indefinite wait.

- An in-flight request is bounded by the 120 s global timeout, which includes the body read. A cancel during a wait is seen within 100 ms; a cancel during an in-flight request is seen when that request returns. Both are documented.
Transport and secret handling checks:

- HTTPS-only holds in every build. Endpoint::parse accepts only https, UreqTransport::send refuses a non-https endpoint, and the agent has https_only(true). The loopback constructors exist only under the test-util feature, and Endpoint::loopback_http can only build http://127.0.0.1:port.

- Redirects are not followed. In ureq 3.5.1, max_redirects_do_error() is `max_redirects > 0 && will_error`, so with 0 redirects a 3xx is returned as a response and not an error. This agrees with test_redirects_are_not_followed.
- The response cap is 8 MiB. The body is read through take(cap + 1) and refused if it exceeds the cap. This applies to success and error statuses (tests at ureq.rs:155).

- Every Err from send_with_busy_retry is redacted in one place (retry.rs:246) through ResolvedApiKey::redact_error. That covers errors from third-party Transport impls and all JevError text variants. tests/retry.rs test_transport_error_with_secret_is_redacted checks it.

- SecretHeader Debug shows ResolvedApiKey([redacted]), and HttpRequest Debug shows only the body length. I found no tracing, println! or dbg! in the HTTP code. The panics I saw (expect and assert messages) contain no secret.
- The backends and Jev client redact their own error paths as well: http_failure (a 300-byte body snippet) and the parse errors. Jev's non-200 error carries only the status.

- The loopback test server (tests/support/mod.rs) has no unbounded waits. The accept loop is nonblocking with a 30 s deadline, each stream has 10 s read and write timeouts, a stalled reply releases on finish() or at 30 s, and finish() waits at most 10 s.
Observations (below Important, not findings):

(1) JevClientConfig::new accepts attempts 1..=8 and timeout up to 3600 s (crates/sc-jev/src/config.rs:105-109). The packaged jev.toml uses 4 sends and 60 s, so the defaults are compliant. But the public JevClient::with_config path lets a caller exceed the owner decisions of at most 4 sends and 120 s in flight. Consider tightening to 1..=4 and <=120 s. The haiku and luna backends are unaffected because they use BusyPolicy::default and Timeouts::default.

(2) The wait is capped to the remaining budget, so the last attempt can start at exactly t = 90 s. The test test_retry_sleep_capped_by_budget asserts this deliberately. The budget is checked only after a busy reply, so a slow first send can still run to 120 s. This is consistent with the owner wording "budget on starting attempts".

(3) The "double-charge" rationale is not stated in the docs. retry.rs and the tests say that an error after the body was sent is not retried, but nothing mentions the double-billing reason. A one-line doc note would match the owner intent.

(4) SecretHeader::matches is public in all builds, not only under test-util. It is an equality oracle that needs a candidate key, so it is not a leak. The module docs say it is intended for test transports.
(5) A busy reply with an oversize body (over 8 MiB) surfaces as RESPONSE_INVALID and is not retried. That is acceptable.
(6) test_util's RecordingTransport and ScriptedTransport Debug output prints recorded requests. The secret is redacted through the HttpRequest Debug, so there is no leak.
